observations: A large rounded head shape sits against a flat saturated yellow background, its surface covered in overlapping lines in green, blue, red, purple, gray, and black that leave almost no white area unpatterned.
Two eye sockets are outlined in thick green loops; each contains a white rectangle with a short red horizontal mark at center, giving both eyes the same flat, forward-facing quality.
A wide open mouth near the bottom shows a row of white rectangular teeth outlined in black, framed by a red lip line, with the lower jaw visibly offset slightly left of the face's vertical center.
reading: Dense overlapping lines in many colors pack the face's surface until the underlying form reads more as a container than a volume. The two eyes, identical in their red-mark-on-white construction, suggest a mask worn rather than a face inhabited. That wide tooth-filled mouth reads as a grin or a grimace depending on how long you look — the yellow field around it stays warm and loud, refusing to settle the question.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors #80 and #82. Where #80 uses broad color fills and a scalloped outer edge, #81 replaces those calmer zones with wall-to-wall line density — the quality the collector links to scrimshaw's tightly worked surfaces.

connections.reason: Both works use a frontal face with rectangular eye sockets and a tooth-row mouth, but #80 relies on large flat color fills and a scalloped outer edge where #81 covers the same structure with dense overlapping line work.

Title neighbor #82 also places rectangular eye frames with cross marks on a flat ground, but its near-black face mass against pink produces a stark two-tone contrast that #81's multicolor line density does not share.

lookingQuestion: The two eye marks are nearly identical in construction — does that sameness make the face feel more symmetrical or more unsettled to you?
ambiguities: The nnotb #30 comparison image shows a full skeletal figure on a teal ground with no close formal parallel to this face-only composition; no connection was selected.
Title order and recorded creation order align for this work, but the metadata notes gaps may exist elsewhere in the owned subset, so adjacency is not confirmed as a making sequence.
